reader.requirement: At --std 85 the break test compares each control item with its saved prior as a relation condition: a numeric item as two numeric operands (so -0 equals +0), an index data item as two index data items, any other item (alphanumeric, group, edited) as two nonnumeric operands under the program collating sequence.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.ControlOperandMayBeIndexDataItem (Year < 2002) admits an index data item as CONTROL operand only at 85; ControlOperandShapeViolation refuses it from 2002 (§2023:13.18.60.3 SR10)
emits the engine's Edition from DialectLevel; the index-item arm (value key) is reachable only at 85 because the binder admits it only there

reader.edition-search: the numeric (NumericControlEqual), float and collated-nonnumeric arms in EmitReportConstruction switch on category/usage only; grep for DialectLevel/Edition in the control loop finds none besides the emitted Edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 3b (index data item control) exists only at 85; at 2023 the same program is refused (COBOL1700, §2023:13.18.60.3 SR10). The numeric and nonnumeric arms are the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb5782_numeric_control_signed_zero covers 3a (zoned separate-sign and packed -0); not 3b (index item) or 3c (group, program collating sequence)

probes.printed: 3c: KB A->B with ALPHABET A1 IS "A" ALSO "B" as PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE: no break; A->C: break. 3c group: GRP holding +0 -> -0 image (GK = 0 true): CF-GRP printed. 3b: IX 1->1 no break, 1->3 break, CF-IX sees prior 1, TERMINATE 3
--std 2023 --compile-only: error COBOL1700 RD 'R3': CONTROL operand 'IX' is an index data item
probes.expected: a later edition refuses the 85-only index control

reader.notes: The emitter picks the comparison by the item's class: image-carried numeric -> NumericControlEqual (value), index -> occurrence-number key, float -> value/bit key, otherwise the collated StrCompare when a program collating sequence is in effect, else ordinal equality of equal-length images. A group containing a signed zero breaks on the sign image, as the nonnumeric comparison requires.

refuter.evidence: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-234/r4ctl.cob uses PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE A1 IS "1" ALSO "2" ... Numeric KN PIC 9 going 1->2 breaks: the numeric test ignores the alphabet (3a). Numeric-edited KE PIC Z9 going ' 1'->' 2' does not break, and ' 1'->' 3' does: KE is not a numeric data item, so the nonnumeric test applies under the collating sequence (3c). Signed zoned KT going from +0 to the overpunch -0 '}' does not break (3a, numeric equality). The 85 refusal of VALUE 1 on an edited item (COBOL0900) also confirmed the edition gate. The index item (3b) and the group (3c) are covered by the reader's p4ctl. cite.py: `OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.4 GR3c  ... the text is in GR3c`.
